# The premise row is published but no reviewer in neo loads it

## Context

`neo-agent-skills@0.1.7` published 2026-09-15, carrying the graduated-decision-reversal premise row from `neo-agent-skills#7` (a sub of #16212). Verified in the published tarball, not inferred from the version:

```
npm pack neo-agent-skills@0.1.7 → package/.agents/skills/pr-review/audits/cycle-1-premise-preflight.md
  "Graduated-decision reversal | Does the diff amend or reverse a graduated decision …"  present
  #16188 anchor                                                                          present
  "not an ADR-edit ban" legality note                                                     present
```

**It reaches nobody here.** Measured on `dev`:

| pin | value |
|---|---|
| registry `latest` | **0.1.7** ✅ |
| `devDependencies.neo-agent-skills` | **0.1.6** |
| `.github/workflows/pr-baseline.yml:73` reusable-workflow SHA | **`@6b009521…`** (pre-release) |
| the **installed** corpus at `node_modules/neo-agent-skills/.agents/skills/…` | row **absent** |

`.agents/skills` in this repository is a symlink into `node_modules`, so the dependency pin *is* what an agent loads. Until it moves, every Cycle-1 review here runs against a catalog without the row — the exact reviewer this row was written for cannot see it.

## The Problem

**"Published" and "runs here" are different facts, and only the second governs.** This is the third instance today of that same gap biting a real lane: the archaeology guard's entity fix shipped in `0.1.5` while this repo pinned `0.1.4` (#18729's revert trigger), and I recorded the trigger as two conditions when it had three — having collapsed *published* into *consumed*.

The consequence here is quiet rather than red. Nothing fails; the row simply is not in the substrate, so no reviewer cites it, and the retirement question `neo-agent-skills#7` scoped out — *"if the row proves load-bearing"* — cannot even be asked, because it has had no chance to fire.

## The Architectural Reality

The org already settled the shape: **consumers pin, and the pin move is a deliberate, reviewed step.** Precedent commits for the `0.1.5` move, both under #16553:

- `b3651efafc chore(deps): neo-agent-skills 0.1.5, and the two colour escapes come out (#16553)`
- `367b8b565e ci(baseline): the reusable workflow pin moves to the release that carries the rules (#16553)`

Two pins, two commits, one ticket. This ticket is the `0.1.7` instance of that same move. #16553 is CLOSED/COMPLETED and had a PR, so it cannot host this.

**Why the immutable SHA pin is right and must move too:** `pr-baseline.yml` calls the reusable workflow at a commit SHA, which is why publishing `0.1.7` broke nothing — the shared workflow this repo actually runs is still the `0.1.6`-pinned revision. That safety is also why the row cannot arrive on its own.

## The Fix

Three coordinated moves, mirroring the #16553 precedent:

1. `package.json` — `devDependencies.neo-agent-skills` `0.1.6` → `0.1.7`
2. `package-lock.json` + the install, via `npm install neo-agent-skills@0.1.7`
3. `.github/workflows/pr-baseline.yml:73` — reusable-workflow SHA `6b009521fac6f571be2200cadbeab734cfcffe6d` → `9ed944a05becfd4759ea34681c6c479dc3d3b614` (skills `dev` HEAD, the `#73` merge, which carries `SKILLS_VERSION: '0.1.7'` at all three of its own pin sites)

## Decision Record impact

`none`. A consumer dependency move along an established route; no contract, no guard logic, no policy change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `devDependencies.neo-agent-skills` reads `0.1.7`, and `package-lock.json` agrees.
- [ ] The **installed** corpus contains the row — asserted against `node_modules/neo-agent-skills/.agents/skills/pr-review/audits/cycle-1-premise-preflight.md`, not against the registry or the lockfile. This is the AC that distinguishes *consumed* from *published*, and it is the one the earlier two-condition mistake would have skipped.
- [ ] `pr-baseline.yml`'s reusable-workflow SHA resolves to a skills commit whose three `SKILLS_VERSION` pins read `0.1.7`.
- [ ] `PR Baseline` is green on this PR — the moved SHA is exercised by the PR that moves it, so the new workflow revision proves itself before merge rather than after.
- [ ] No other dependency moves in the same diff.

## Out of Scope

- `neo-agent-skills#14` (unify PR governance across repositories) — the architecture question of *who owns policy and required contexts*. This is the routine per-release move under the existing arrangement, not a change to it.
- #17783 — narrowed by its own body to the R2/R3 policy-tool/caller leaf, *"and nothing else"*; @neo-opus-grace holds it.
- Other consumers (Brain, Institution, DevIndex). @neo-opus-grace ran the `0.1.6` org-wide sweep and this repo is one row of the `0.1.7` one.
- Whether the premise row earns mechanical validation — `neo-agent-skills#7`'s Out of Scope owns that, and it needs the row loaded first.

## Avoided Traps

**A lockfile is not an install.** This checkout had `package-lock.json` at `0.1.6` while `node_modules` carried `0.1.4`. Asserting the lockfile would have passed while the loaded corpus stayed two releases stale — so AC-2 reads the installed file.

**A version bump is not one edit.** In the skills repo the release moves `package.json` **and three** `SKILLS_VERSION` pins, asserted separately as package / substrate / PR-body drift. The consumer side has its own multiplicity: dependency pin, lockfile, install, and the workflow SHA. Moving one and calling it done is the same shape of miss.

**Do not read the registry as evidence of local state.** `npm view` answers what is published. The reviewer-facing question is what `.agents/skills` resolves to through the symlink.
